newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Fraud costs Argentine firms $8.5 bln a year - study.
newsitem.headline: Fraud costs Argentine firms $8.5 bln a year - study.

text.p: Fraud committed from within companies cost Argentine firms about $8.5 billion a year, pollsters Mora y Araujo said Monday.
Mora y Araujo's director of labor studies, Ernesto Kritz, said the amount, gleaned from a poll of 80 corporate presidents, represents about two percent of all transactions.
"We were astonished by the amount," Kritz told Reuters.
Kritz said about half of those consulted have not answered and that the poll is not yet complete.
Final results will be announced later this month at a seminar in Buenos Aires organizaed by Mora y Araujo and consultants KPMG.
A KPMG study in eight developed countries showed 97 percent of corporate managers considered corruption a key issue, but only 20 percent know of potential fraud in their firms.

Mario Kutnowski, director for Human Resources at KPMG, said in an interview: "It is amazing the lack of knowledge among the the public and companies' leaders who have a general knowledge of the issue, but who don't know how it works."
The KPMG study showed that an official body in New Zealand probed 45 fraud cases for a total of $500 million in four years. Sixty percent of the firms involved went bankrupt.
Most common activities include lying to bosses, falsifying documents and theft.
